proposals.before: Qin established Ying as the Nangun commandery.
proposals.after: Qin established Ying as the Nanjun commandery.
proposals.reason: 南郡 is the place name Nanjun (Nan Commandery), not the fused form “Nangun.”

proposals.before: Qin made Ying into Nanhun Commandery.
proposals.after: Qin made Ying into Nan Commandery.
proposals.reason: 南郡 means Nan Commandery; “Nanhun” is a mistransliteration.

proposals.before: The walls held firm and could not be entered. Meanwhile, Qin's 25,000 surprise soldiers cut off Zhao's rear, and another force of 5,000 cavalry cut across Zhao's walls. Zhao's forces was divided in two, and their grain route was cut.
proposals.after: The walls held firm and could not be entered. Meanwhile, Qin's 25,000 surprise soldiers cut off Zhao's rear, and another force of 5,000 cavalry cut across Zhao's walls. Zhao's forces were divided in two, and their grain route was cut.
proposals.reason: The plural subject “forces” requires the plural verb “were.”

proposals.before: Kuo's forces was defeated. 400,000 soldiers surrendered to Lord Wu'an.
proposals.after: Kuo's forces were defeated. 400,000 soldiers surrendered to Lord Wu'an.
proposals.reason: The plural subject “forces” requires the plural verb “were.”

proposals.before: Chu dispatched Lord Chunshen and Wei sent its prince to lead several hundred thousand troops to attack the Qin forces. The Qin forces suffered heavy casualties.
proposals.after: Chu dispatched Lord Chunshen and the Prince of Wei to lead several hundred thousand troops to attack the Qin forces. The Qin forces suffered heavy casualties.
proposals.reason: 楚使 governs both 春申君 and 魏公子; the current translation incorrectly introduces Wei as a second sending agent.

proposals.before: Wang Jian was a man from the eastern village of Fenyin.
proposals.after: Wang Jian was a man from the eastern village of Pinyang.
proposals.reason: 頻陽 is Pinyang here, matching the Chinese place name and the idiomatic translation.

proposals.before: Wang Jian's counsel was not heeded, so he pleaded illness and returned to retire in Fenyin.
proposals.after: Wang Jian's counsel was not heeded, so he pleaded illness and returned to retire in Pinyang.
proposals.reason: 頻陽 is Pinyang, not Fenyin.

proposals.before: Wang Jian's advice was not used, so he claimed illness and returned to retire in Fenyin.
proposals.after: Wang Jian's advice was not used, so he claimed illness and returned to retire in Pinyang.
proposals.reason: 頻陽 is Pinyang, not Fenyin.

proposals.before: Shihuang heard of it and grew greatly angry. He raced personally to Fenyin and apologized to Wang Jian: 'I did not use your plan. Li Xin has indeed disgraced our Qin forces.
proposals.after: Shihuang heard of it and grew greatly angry. He raced personally to Pinyang and apologized to Wang Jian: 'I did not use your plan. Li Xin has indeed disgraced our Qin forces.
proposals.reason: 頻陽 is Pinyang, not Fenyin.

proposals.before: Shihuang heard of it and grew greatly angry. He raced personally to Fenyin and apologized to Wang Jian: 'I did not use your plan. Li Xin has indeed disgraced our Qin army.
proposals.after: Shihuang heard of it and grew greatly angry. He raced personally to Pinyang and apologized to Wang Jian: 'I did not use your plan. Li Xin has indeed disgraced our Qin army.
proposals.reason: 頻陽 is Pinyang, not Fenyin.

proposals.before: After a long time, Wang Jian sent someone to ask if the forces was playing.
proposals.after: After a long time, Wang Jian sent someone to ask if the forces were playing.
proposals.reason: The plural subject “forces” requires the plural verb “were.”

proposals.before: Reaching south of Qi, he slew their general Xiang Yan. Chu soldiers thereupon fled in rout.
proposals.after: Reaching south of Qian, he slew their general Xiang Yan. Chu soldiers thereupon fled in rout.
proposals.reason: 蘄 is the place Qian in this translation context, not the state name Qi.

proposals.before: Reaching south of Qi, he killed their general Xiang Yan. Chu soldiers fled in defeat.
proposals.after: Reaching south of Qian, he killed their general Xiang Yan. Chu soldiers fled in defeat.
proposals.reason: 蘄 is the place Qian in this translation context, not the state name Qi.

proposals.before: When Chen Sheng rebelled against Qin, Qin sent Wang Jian's grandson Wang Li to attack Zhao, besieging King Zhao of Qin and Zhang Er at Julu City.
proposals.after: When Chen Sheng rebelled against Qin, Qin sent Wang Jian's grandson Wang Li to attack Zhao, besieging the King of Zhao and Zhang Er at Julu City.
proposals.reason: 趙王 is the King of Zhao, not a Qin king; 'King Zhao of Qin' invents the wrong polity.

decisions.reason: 秦以郢為南郡 names the commandery 南郡 (Nanjun); “Nangun” is a wrong romanization, and “Nanjun commandery” restores the correct reading.
南郡 is Nan Commandery; “Nanhun” misreads the place name, and “Nan Commandery” matches the Chinese.
趙軍分而為二 is rendered with plural “forces,” which requires “were,” not “was”; the proposal fixes only that agreement error.
括軍敗 uses plural “forces” in English, so the verb must be “were”; the rest of the sentence matches 卒四十萬人降武安君.
楚使春申君及魏公子 has one verb 使 governing both objects joined by 及; the original wrongly adds Wei as a second sender, and “Chu dispatched Lord Chunshen and the Prince of Wei” restores that syntax.
頻陽東鄉 is Pinyang’s eastern village; “Fenyin” (汾陰) is a different place, and “Pinyang” matches 頻陽 and the idiomatic line.
歸老於頻陽 means he retired to Pinyang; “Fenyin” misnames 頻陽.
The same 歸老於頻陽 requires Pinyang in the literal; “Fenyin” is incorrect.
自馳如頻陽 means Shihuang raced to Pinyang; “Fenyin” misreads 頻陽.
Literal 自馳如頻陽 likewise requires Pinyang, not Fenyin.
Plural “forces” translating 軍中 requires “were playing”; the proposal corrects only the subject–verb error.
至蘄南 is south of the place 蘄 (Qian), not the state 齊 (Qi); “south of Qian” restores the correct toponym.
The same 蘄南 in the literal is Qian, not Qi; the proposed replacement is accurate.
圍趙王及張耳 means the King of Zhao, not a Qin king; “King Zhao of Qin” invents the wrong polity, and “the King of Zhao” matches 趙王.
